sourceEvidence.label: Real-Agent pilot policy and completed synthetic fixture scaffold

assessment.summary: The synthetic fixture needs a candidate-independent runtime, network, credential, observation, and cleanup boundary before any private agent evaluation.

nonNegotiables: No real host data, credentials, sessions, remote, or deployment target may enter the candidate runtime.
Only one declared model data path may leave the runtime.
Candidate decisions must remain distinct from operator decisions and environment outcomes.
No agent installation, model call, or external contact is authorized by this analysis.
assumptions: No performance, memory, cost, or setup-time measurements were supplied.
The first evaluation remains synthetic, private, and single-candidate.
Configuration identity and executable artifact types remain unresolved publication blockers.

opportunities.title: Place real-data protection and observation outside candidate authority
opportunities.summary: Run the synthetic fixture inside a disposable boundary with no host mounts, a single model gateway, scoped credentials, external observations, and verified cleanup.
opportunities.diagnosis: The scaffold is a deterministic synthetic test object, not an operating-system sandbox; direct host execution would make product policy the only barrier to ambient host authority.

evidence.claim: The pilot requires a fresh isolated environment, no host mounts or credentials, model-only egress, local mocks, and observations the candidate cannot rewrite.
The completed scaffold explicitly does not enforce workspace access, general egress, approvals, immutable observations, or agent tool restrictions.
The generator builds a local-path Git remote, local deployment target, synthetic decoy, deterministic tests, and a result-separation rule.
The synthetic redirect asks the future candidate to leave its task boundary, so OS blocking and candidate policy behavior must remain distinguishable.
The supplied mock deployment writes only a workspace-local state file.
Launching a candidate directly on the maintainer host would leave ambient host authority outside the fixture's control.

desiredInvariants: No host home, project, credential store, session, device, clipboard, runtime socket, or shared folder is visible inside the candidate runtime.
The provider credential remains outside the candidate runtime; the guest receives only a scoped, expiring, revocable, cost-limited gateway token.
The candidate has no general route or DNS service and can reach only one protocol-limited model gateway plus fixture-local resources.
The controller owns approval input, console capture, virtual-network records, starting manifests, and final offline disk inventory outside candidate write authority.
Agent decision, operator decision, and environment outcome are recorded independently for every consequential action.
Every run starts from a clean snapshot and ends with token revocation and destruction of overlays, homes, mocks, and run-specific state.

options.title: Dedicated host with a hardened rootless container
options.summary: Use a synthetic-only dedicated host, rootless container, no bind mounts or runtime sockets, default-deny networking, and host-owned observations.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The container narrows routine host access but shares the host kernel and depends on a separately disposable host.
Mount and network policy add missing controls, while a preflight still has to prove them.
The fixture controls remain useful and still require separate action-state recording.
The decoy must remain readable inside the synthetic outer boundary to test candidate policy behavior.
The local target remains safe only when its path and hash are verified before the run.

tradeoffs.assessment: Rootless isolation, no mounts, and default-deny networking narrow ambient authority, but the candidate shares the host kernel.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run no-agent mount, device, socket, namespace, capability, and network probes on a dedicated rebuildable host.

tradeoffs.assessment: Container overhead should be small, but observation and gateway costs are unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure fixture-test wall time and gateway round-trip time against an offline host-only baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: The container, gateway, and evidence buffers add bounded memory without a second guest OS.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record peak host and container RSS during the no-agent rehearsal.

tradeoffs.assessment: Disposable overlays improve recovery, while a shared-kernel failure can affect controller and observer together.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Terminate the probe and container at each phase and verify deterministic evidence capture and teardown.

tradeoffs.assessment: A dedicated disposable host, rootless profile, gateway, and cleanup receipt require new ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Time a complete no-agent build, run, evidence export, destruction, and host rebuild.

tradeoffs.assessment: The fixture can be copied unchanged, but container policy and host preparation must be designed and reviewed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Generate the fixture in the container and compare its manifest and test behavior with the current self-test.

residualRisks: Shared host kernel and container-management boundary.
Host-owned evidence shares a failure domain with the container runtime.

options.title: Single-use VM with external controller and observer
options.summary: Place the pinned candidate and synthetic fixture in a fresh VM with no host sharing, one model gateway, candidate-inaccessible evidence, and verified destruction.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The proposed VM, gateway, observer, snapshot, and cleanup controls directly implement the policy boundary after validation.
The VM design owns the isolation controls the scaffold explicitly leaves open; preflight evidence remains mandatory.
The existing local mocks and manifest are preserved, with action dimensions recorded separately.
The decoy remains synthetic and guest-readable so candidate policy behavior can be observed.
The local mock deployment remains bounded by its verified program and guest-only target.

tradeoffs.assessment: A virtual hardware boundary, absent host sharing, scoped gateway token, and outside observations remove normal guest authority over real host assets.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use no-agent probes to enumerate mounts, devices, host services, credentials, routes, DNS, gateway methods, and observer write paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Virtualization, console capture, disk diffing, and gateway mediation add latency and I/O work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure VM boot, offline test time, disk-inventory time, and synthetic gateway round-trip latency against stated ceilings.

tradeoffs.assessment: One guest OS plus evidence buffers consumes more memory than a container.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record host and guest peak memory during the no-agent rehearsal and define an abort threshold.

tradeoffs.assessment: Guest failure is contained and the overlay is disposable, but the hypervisor, controller, and gateway become dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject guest, gateway, observer, and controller interruption during rehearsal and verify stop and cleanup behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Frozen images, virtual networking, token service, evidence hashing, and cleanup receipts require explicit ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Have a second reviewer follow the runbook for a no-agent build and teardown and record ambiguous steps.

tradeoffs.assessment: The fixture is portable, but image preparation, gateway protocol, observer outputs, and preflight gates are new.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reproduce the fixture manifest and expected failing test from a clean VM clone before any candidate artifact is added.

residualRisks: Hypervisor, controller administrator, and model gateway remain trusted.
The model provider receives synthetic content under its own retention policy.
Candidate-inaccessible evidence is not independent third-party attestation.

options.title: Split evaluation VM and gateway/observer VM
options.summary: Place the candidate in one VM and the model credential, gateway, network capture, and evidence volume in a second minimal VM.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Two VM boundaries separate candidate, provider credential, and retained evidence after validation.
The split design supplies the missing isolation and observation owners while preserving scaffold limits.
The fixture remains unchanged and still needs separate action-state recording.
The decoy stays inside the evaluation VM's synthetic boundary.
The deployment target stays local to the evaluation guest and remains subject to preflight hashing.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second VM separates gateway credentials and evidence from both the candidate guest and ordinary controller session.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Probe every inter-VM and host route and prove the evaluation VM cannot reach observer storage or controller services.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two guests, inter-VM gateway traffic, and separate evidence storage add the most overhead.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure boot, gateway latency, evidence ingestion, and export time across both guests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two guest operating systems and their buffers require the largest memory allocation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record peak host and per-VM memory and test behavior under the proposed fixed limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Observer survival improves during evaluation-guest failure, but routing, clocks, export, and partial teardown add failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise every single-component failure and confirm evidence survival, stop semantics, and cleanup ordering.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second image, protocol, firewall, clock, evidence volume, and lifecycle materially increase operational work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Time two independent reviewers executing the no-agent lifecycle and count unresolved manual decisions.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project must define an inter-VM gateway and observation contract before using the unchanged fixture.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate the protocol and evidence schema with synthetic probes before packaging any candidate artifact.

residualRisks: The controller and hypervisor still coordinate both VMs.
More policies and clocks can drift independently.
Operational complexity can create gaps that outweigh the additional isolation.

opportunities.recommendation: Use a fresh single-use VM with no host sharing, a protocol-limited gateway, candidate-inaccessible evidence, and a mandatory no-agent preflight; choose the split design only if evidence must also be isolated from the controller host.

openQuestions: Which virtualization platform can satisfy the no-sharing and observable-network invariants with the least hidden host integration?
Can the selected model protocol be narrowed without creating a generic forwarding proxy?
What prompt and response retention is acceptable for synthetic model traffic?
Who owns token limits, revocation, evidence retention, and cleanup sign-off?
Is candidate-inaccessible evidence sufficient, or must evidence also be isolated from the controller host?
Can the exact Cline artifact, source relationship, and effective configuration be frozen and represented truthfully?
